stem: In the figure, line \(\ell\) is parallel to line \(m\). Point \(A\) lies on line \(\ell\), and points \(B\) and \(C\) lie on line \(m\). What is the value of \(x\)?
solution: The 52°, \(x^{\circ}\), and 63° angles at \(A\) together form a straight angle along line \(\ell\).
(Equivalently: by alternate interior angles, angle \(ABC = 52^{\circ}\) and angle \(ACB = 63^{\circ}\), and the triangle's angles add up to 180°.)

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is \(180 - 52\), which ignores the 63° angle. The three angles at \(A\) along line \(\ell\) add up to 180°.
explanation.B: Correct. Angles \(B\) and \(C\) of the triangle are 52° and 63°, so \(x = 180 - 115 = 65\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the measure of angle \(ABC\), which equals the 52° angle at \(A\) by alternate interior angles; it is not angle \(BAC\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is \(52 + 63\), the sum of the other two angles of the triangle. It still must be subtracted from 180.

verify:
choices = {o: choices[n] for o, n in {'D': 'A', 'B': 'B', 'A': 'C', 'C': 'D'}.items()}; answer = {'A': 'D', 'B': 'B', 'C': 'A', 'D': 'C'}[answer]  # shuffled: original letters
P=figure['points']
d=lambda a,b: sqrt((P[a][0]-P[b][0])**2+(P[a][1]-P[b][1])**2)
ang=lambda a,v,b: N(acos(((P[a][0]-P[v][0])*(P[b][0]-P[v][0])+(P[a][1]-P[v][1])*(P[b][1]-P[v][1]))/(d(a,v)*d(b,v)))*180/pi)
assert P['L1'][1]==P['L2'][1]==P['A'][1] and P['M1'][1]==P['M2'][1]==P['B'][1]==P['C'][1]
assert abs(ang('L1','A','B')-52)<0.1 and abs(ang('L2','A','C')-63)<0.1
ans=180-52-63
assert abs(ang('B','A','C')-ans)<0.1
assert value(choices[answer])==ans
assert all(value(choices[k])!=ans for k in choices if k!=answer)
